title: Integral realization of a Frobenius factor
statement:
Let $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$ be a smooth-proper datum [def-weil-smooth-proper-datum] over the finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and fix an indeterminate $T$. For every prime $\ell\neq p$ write $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$ for the field of $\ell$-adic numbers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], and let $P_{i,\ell}(T)\in\Ql[T]$, $0\leq i\leq2d$, be the determinant factors $P_{i,\ell}(T)=\det(1-TF_{i,\ell}\mid H^i(X,\Ql))$ of the smooth-proper cohomological family of $\mathscr X$ [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family]. For $P=\sum_{r\geq0}c_rT^r$ in the polynomial ring $\mathbf Z[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] write $P^{(\ell)}=\sum_{r\geq0}(c_r\cdot1_{\Ql})T^r\in\Ql[T]$ for its coefficientwise extension [def-weil-coefficientwise-extension].

For an integer $i$ with $0\leq i\leq2d$ and a polynomial $P\in\mathbf Z[T]$, the proposition '$P$ is an integral realization-independent factor of $\mathscr X$ in degree $i$' is

$$
\forall\,\ell\text{ prime},\ \ell\neq p:\qquad P^{(\ell)}=P_{i,\ell}\quad\text{in }\Ql[T].
$$

This defines a predicate on $\mathbf Z[T]$ (depending on $\mathscr X$ and $i$), and nothing more: the identity is required for every prime $\ell\neq p$ simultaneously, not for one fixed $\ell$, and the definition asserts neither that such a $P$ exists nor that it is unique. Existence (with normalization $P(0)=1$) and uniqueness are the theorem prop-integral-recovery, and the polynomial so obtained is named by def-weil-canonical-integral-factors.

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against its source (master blueprint, order 2857; slopmaster2 has no copy: its TeX states only the existence theorem, 01_statement_final.tex:134 and 14_integrality_final.tex:237 thm:integral-frobenius-factors). The mathematical content is kept: for each i, a P in Z[T] with P^(l)=P_{i,l} for every prime l != p. The statement was rewritten to (1) introduce its objects through the reviewed smooth-proper datum X=(X_0,d,X), as def-weil-canonical-integral-factors does, (2) name every notion it is built from: the finite-field datum (def-weil-finite-field-fiber, kept), the smooth-proper datum (def-weil-smooth-proper-datum, added; replaces def-weil-geometric-hypotheses, removed, which the datum already carries), Q_l (def-weil-l-adic-numbers, added, Mathlib leaf), the determinant factors P_{i,l} (def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family, kept), Z[T] (def-weil-polynomial-ring, added, Mathlib leaf) and P^(l) (def-weil-coefficientwise-extension, added, Mathlib leaf; previously defined inline), and (3) separate definition from theorem as the reviewers asked: the node now defines a predicate on Z[T] quantified over every prime l != p, and says explicitly that it asserts neither existence nor uniqueness, which are prop-integral-recovery (with P(0)=1), and that the resulting polynomial is def-weil-canonical-integral-factors. prop-integral-recovery is mentioned in the text but not made a statement dependency: the predicate does not need it, and prop-integral-recovery and def-weil-canonical-integral-factors already depend on this node (making it a dependency would create a cycle). No new node was needed: every notion already has a node. Primes l, the quantifier over l != p and the range 0<=i<=2d are judged elementary (Nat.Prime). Mathlib search: no match for the node; it is one line over Mathlib once the family P_{i,l} is given.
